types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign state recognized by the international community Also called Nation, State, CountryTerritory, GeopoliticalEntity. Examples: Ukraine, Russia, Ukrainian, Ukraine's government.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Ukraine and Russia are recognized sovereign states matching schema.org's Country definition.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Refinery: A facility where crude oil is processed into usable petroleum products Also called OilProcessingPlant, PetroleumRefinery, HydrocarbonRefinery, EnergyFacility. Examples: Bashneft-Novoil refinery, Slavneft-Yanos refinery, Bashneft-Novoil, refinery in Bashkortostan.

chosen_type.label: OilRefinery
chosen_type.definition: A facility where crude oil is processed into usable petroleum products
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate matches the specific function of oil refining; minting to capture distinct industrial purpose.

candidates.label: GasStation
candidates.comment: A GasStation is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells fuel for vehicles. Also called petrol station, filling station, service station. Examples: Shell, ExxonMobil, a local independent gas station.

candidates.label: EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration indicating whether a product is EnergyStar certified. Also called Energy Star rating, Energy Star certification. Examples: EnergyStarCertified, NotEnergyStarCertified.

candidates.label: AutoRepair
candidates.comment: An AutoRepair is an AutomotiveBusiness that provides mechanical maintenance and repair services for vehicles. Also called car mechanic, garage, auto service center, vehicle workshop. Examples: Jiffy Lube, a local independent mechanic, a dealership service department. Distinct from AutoBodyShop, which focuses on exterior and structural damage.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: RecyclingCenter
candidates.comment: A RecyclingCenter is a LocalBusiness providing facilities for recycling waste materials. Also called recycling facility, waste collection center. Examples: a municipal recycling center, a bottle and can redemption center, an electronics recycling drop-off, a hazardous waste collection site.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being with a distinct identity Also called Individual, Figure, PublicPerson, GovernmentOfficial. Examples: President Volodymyr Zelensky, Mikhail Evraev, Isik Mater, Zelensky.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: President Volodymyr Zelensky and Mikhail Evraev are individual human beings fitting schema.org's Person class.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement Also called UrbanCenter, MunicipalArea, Metropolis, Settlement. Examples: Kherson, Balakliya, Lozova, Odesa.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: Kherson, Balakliya, Lozova, and Odesa are all large permanent human settlements matching schema.org's City definition.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: SubwayStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a stop or terminal for subway or metro trains. Also called metro station, underground station, tube station. Examples: 'Grand Central Terminal', 'London Underground station', 'Tokyo Metro station'.

types.embedding_query_text: Region: A large and relatively distinct area within a country Also called AdministrativeRegion, TerritorialDivision, SubnationalArea, GovernanceArea. Examples: Bashkortostan, Yaroslavl, Kharkiv region, Dnipropetrovsk region.

chosen_type.label: AdministrativeArea
chosen_type.justification: Bashkortostan, Yaroslavl, Kharkiv region, and Dnipropetrovsk region are all administrative divisions within countries.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

chosen_type.label: DateTime
chosen_type.justification: 2026-08-05T20:00:00 is a specific point in time with both date and time components as defined by schema.org's DateTime.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: OpeningHoursSpecification
candidates.comment: An OpeningHoursSpecification, as a StructuredValue, provides information about the opening hours of a place or service. Also called business hours, operating hours, schedule. Examples: 'Mon-Fri 9am-5pm', 'Open 24/7', 'Closed on Sundays'. Distinct from Event, which describes a specific occurrence.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: 2026-08-05 and 2022-02-24 are calendar dates without time components matching schema.org's Date definition.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

chosen_type.label: Distance
chosen_type.justification: 1,300km and 700km are numerical values with units of length fitting schema.org's Distance class.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: PostalCodeRangeSpecification
candidates.comment: A PostalCodeRangeSpecification is a StructuredValue indicating a range of postal codes, defined by a beginning and ending code. Also called zip code range, postcode boundary. Examples: 90210-90215, 00000-99999, a range of postal codes for a delivery zone.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

chosen_type.label: Number
chosen_type.justification: 93, 11, 4, 66,000, and 605 are all pure numerical values matching schema.org's Number data type.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".

candidates.label: Enumeration
candidates.comment: An Enumeration is an Intangible representing a list of predefined values or categories. Also called list, category, type. Examples: A list of music genres, a set of clothing sizes, a collection of event statuses.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

candidates.label: ReturnMethodEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various methods available for returning a product. Also called product return options, return types, refund methods. Examples: in-store return, mail-in return, courier pickup, drop-off point.

chosen_type.label: PercentageValue
chosen_type.definition: A numerical value expressed as a percentage
chosen_type.justification: 31% and 69% require a percentage-specific type not present in schema.org candidates.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".

candidates.label: DENonprofitType
candidates.comment: DENonprofitType is an enumeration representing specific types of non-profit organizations recognized under German fiscal code, article 52. Also called German non-profit classification, AO 52 non-profit. Examples: A German charitable foundation, a registered German association for public benefit.

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValueDistribution
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValueDistribution is a StructuredValue representing a statistical distribution of values. Also called value distribution, statistical range. Examples: the average height of a population with standard deviation, a product's price distribution across different retailers, a range of test scores with median and mode.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: UserBlocks
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of blocking another user or content. Also called user block, content block, account block. Examples: a user blocking another user on a social media platform, blocking a specific website, blocking notifications from an app.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: WPAdBlock
candidates.comment: A specific section of a web page dedicated to displaying advertisements. Also called ad unit, advertising block, banner ad section. Examples: a banner ad at the top of a page, a sidebar ad, an interstitial ad space.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.
